title: Cleanup tail bricks SYA.claim(): step 11 deregisters the WRONG (decommissioned, empty 0x3bBE) accumulator, so the old DOLA/USDC strategies stay registered on the live production SYA 0x3C69, and step 12 pausing them reverts the default permissionless claim() for all callers
rootCause: DeregisterOldStrategiesFromSYA.s.sol (step 11) hardcodes LIVE_SYA = 0x3bBE — a decommissioned, EMPTY StableYieldAccumulator instance — instead of the live production accumulator 0x3C69 that step 1 registered the V2 strategies on and step 9 asserts against. Because 0x3bBE's registry is empty, removeYieldStrategy(YS_DOLA_OLD)/removeYieldStrategy(YS_USDC_OLD) are silent no-ops; the owner-equality preflight passes (both SYAs are owner-owned) and the post-asserts pass vacuously (the OLDs are 'absent' from the empty 0x3bBE). The old DOLA/USDC strategies therefore REMAIN registered on the live 0x3C69.
impact: No assets stolen or lost. Step 12 (DecommissionOldStrategies) then pauses YS_DOLA_OLD and YS_USDC_OLD while they are still registered on the live 0x3C69. The default permissionless StableYieldAccumulator.claim(i, m, []) — the path the UI and keepers actually call — iterates registered strategies and skips only on tokenConfig.paused; the old DOLA/USDC TOKEN configs are NOT paused (only the strategy contracts are), so claim() calls skimSurplus() on a paused strategy, hits whenNotPaused, and reverts EnforcedPause. The canonical yield-claim path is bricked for ALL callers until owner action. This is an availability / protocol-function DoS on yield consolidation, not a theft.
attackPath: 1. Operator runs the documented saga in order; step 1 registers the V2 strategies on the live SYA 0x3C69, step 9 asserts against 0x3C69 (all green).
2. Step 11 (DeregisterOldStrategiesFromSYA) hardcodes LIVE_SYA = 0x3bBE (decommissioned, empty); removeYieldStrategy is a silent no-op; owner-equality preflight and post-asserts pass vacuously.
3. The old DOLA/USDC strategies remain registered on the live 0x3C69.
4. Step 12 (DecommissionOldStrategies) pauses YS_DOLA_OLD and YS_USDC_OLD while still registered on 0x3C69.

5. Any claim(i, m, []) iterates registered strategies; SYA skips only on tokenConfig.paused (DOLA/USDC token configs are NOT paused), so it calls skimSurplus() on a paused strategy -> whenNotPaused reverts EnforcedPause -> the entire claim() reverts for everyone.
recommendation: Apply BOTH the immediate address fix and the structural guard so the class cannot recur: (1) Point step 11 LIVE_SYA at the production accumulator 0x3C69 (the same instance step 1 registered the V2 strategies on and step 9 asserts against, matching mainnet-addresses.ts). AND/OR (2) make the guard fail loud rather than vacuous: assert the old strategies are PRESENT on the target SYA BEFORE attempting removeYieldStrategy (so a wrong/empty target reverts instead of no-op'ing), and assert they are DEREGISTERED from the live 0x3C69 BEFORE step 12 pauses them (so the pause can never land on a still-registered strategy). Pin the SYA target against mainnet-addresses.ts rather than a bare in-script constant.
severityRationale: Medium, not High: no funds are stolen or permanently lost — impact is impaired protocol function / availability (the default permissionless yield-claim path is dead). Bounded below High by the exemptStrategies escape hatch: because the paused olds remain registered they are exempt-eligible, so a caller passing [YS_DOLA_OLD, YS_USDC_OLD] routes around the revert, and the owner can fully remediate (re-point step 11 at 0x3C69 and deregister, or unpause). Not Low because the DEFAULT path the UI and keepers call is bricked for all users until owner action — C4 'protocol function or availability impacted'.
footgunRationale: Non-obvious owner footgun (Law 3, in scope): a competent non-malicious operator runs the documented step order and sees a fully green run (owner check + post-asserts all pass) yet has silently bricked the canonical claim path. Surprise => footgun => report; classified by the availability impact, not as malicious-admin. Safe-config guidance: pin step 11 LIVE_SYA to 0x3C69 and assert present-before-remove / deregistered-before-pause (fail loud, not vacuous no-op).
threeLawFraming: Law 1 (no exploits) governs: self-inflicted availability DoS of the permissionless yield-claim path, reached deterministically through the documented runbook by a non-malicious operator. Honest severity Medium: protocol function/availability impacted, no asset theft, owner-remediable, escape hatch exists. Not a Law-2 faithfulness deviation (the story intent is correct; the script targets the wrong address).
relatedNote: Enabled by the guard-design weakness tracked as YS-33 (WeakPreconditionGuard, Low, same DeregisterOldStrategiesFromSYA.s.sol) — kept separate so the assert-present-before-remove remediation survives even if only the address constant is fixed. Distinct from ledger YS-03/44dc0e3a (SYA-not-repointed-to-V2 on the deploy entry, opposite direction: V2 never added; here olds never removed + wrong instance). Distinct from YS-11/6b3c3b98 and YS-12/633f3485.
